mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.2%) compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, indicating economic distress, the S&P 500 tends to decline over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate policy responses and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and retail sales above their 1-month growth thresholds signals strong consumer demand, driving corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% from prior month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 0.5% from prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, characterized by high industrial production growth and low unemployment, the S&P 500 tends to underperform as the economy approaches a peak, leading to negative returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls signals a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS is rising.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI exceeds 2.5%, the S&P 500 tends to decline over the next 20 trading days due to fears of aggressive monetary tightening.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion regime, characterized by rising GDP growth and low unemployment, the S&P 500 tends to outperform as the economy gains momentum, leading to positive returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during early-cycle expansion regimes.
